attempted_claim: Let W be the sibling of the Whitehead link complement (2-cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold). Let C1 be the set of closed 3-manifolds M obtained by Dehn filling both cusps of W along slopes (s1,s2) such that M fibers over the circle with closed genus-2 fiber S and pseudo-Anosov monodromy psi:S->S whose dilatation lambda(psi), defined as the stretch factor equivalently the Perron root of a carrying train-track transition matrix, lies in the fixed patch 1.4656 <= lambda <= 1.75. For each such M let d(M) denote the Hempel distance of its minimal-genus Heegaard splitting, i.e. distance in the curve complex of S between the disk sets of the two handlebodies, with curve-complex and Masur-Minsky subsurface projections as the estimation method. Is it true that every M in C1 is hyperbolic and satisfies d(M) >= 3? A complete answer either proves the bound for every M in C1 with a hyperbolicity certificate, or exhibits one explicit M in C1 with slope pair, monodromy word, verified dilatation in the patch, hyperbolicity certificate, and a weak-reduction or disjoint-disk certificate that d(M) <= 2.
claim_type: universal lower bound with certified-counterexample alternative
decisive_failure: No certified hyperbolicity (flat/degenerate solution types; Sage-backed verification unavailable), no fibered-face or monodromy identification, no verified dilatation in the patch, and no Heegaard-distance certificate were obtained; the boxed census and Fox-calculus factor are routine and uncertified for the target.
